content:
One of my favorite iPhone cases is back with a fresh look. I had used an early version of the BitmoLab GAMEBABY case before, and I fell in love with it at first try. It feels like an accessory specifically designed to evoke my sense of nostalgia. The biggest selling point of this case is that it doesn't require any extra accessories for carrying and charging; instead, it's a cleverly designed regular iPhone case that also doubles as a set of tactile physical buttons, allowing you to play your favorite Game Boy ROM games (and other games). This is the perfect embodiment of "doing it right, without overdoing it." It doesn't need batteries or Bluetooth, and the setup process is very straightforward. If you're a fan of any form of retro game emulators, you should definitely keep an eye on this product.

Check out our hands-on video to see how this case actually performs!

This case is very simple in design yet full of clever ideas. It uses a two-piece design, with the lower half acting as a controller. When you're not gaming daily, the feel is exactly the same as a regular phone case. You can enjoy:

  • Tactile side buttons for the lock button, volume buttons, and action button
  • Cutouts for the USB-C port, speaker, buttons, and camera control
  • Protective bezels surrounding the screen and camera module
  • Hard-shell plastic protection

But the magic is hidden in the lower half. That's where the game's control buttons are, with excellent craftsmanship and a very satisfying tactile feel when pressed. But how exactly does it work?

How It Works

Once again, the cleverness lies in the fact that it has absolutely no built-in electronic components, so no pairing process is required. It works by having each physical game button equipped with a small capacitive contact point that simulates the effect of your finger touching the screen. So the iPhone thinks you're pressing the on-screen control buttons, but it feels like you're pressing real buttons. This uses the same technology as the soft rubber tips of cheap styluses.

You need to go through a simple setup process to ensure the physical buttons align with the control positions on the screen. BitmoLabs provides all the necessary instructions through a QR code in the package. But it requires the Delta emulator app from the App Store to work. This app is completely free to use with zero in-app purchases. After downloading the app, GAMEBABY offers a downloadable custom interface panel that places the emulator's digital control buttons directly under the physical buttons. This panel is also free (you can download it even without the case).

After installing the panel in the Delta emulator app, you're ready to play games. You just need to detach the lower half of the case, flip it over, and reattach it to the iPhone. This way, the control buttons will align with the screen, giving you the feel of real physical buttons when playing retro games. After gaming, just slide out the controller part, flip it over, and snap it back to turn it into a regular phone case again.

My Experience Using It

As I mentioned at the beginning, I'm a slave to retro games—it triggers a deep longing inside me, making me want to replay the old Pokémon games from my youth. This product not only makes gaming easier but also delivers an almost frictionless experience. I don't have to remember to bring any extra items, charge anything, or pair anything. For me, remembering to bring an additional accessory is often the biggest pain point of any tech accessory, and this case eliminates that obstacle.

You can also feel that BitmoLabs has made significant improvements in the craftsmanship of this case. The button rebound feel is excellent, snapping back extremely quickly after release, with no button failure during gameplay. I primarily use it to revisit all the classic Pokémon titles, which are relatively casual games that don't require extremely fast reactions. Even for games that require quick reflexes, this case can absolutely handle it.

There's one trade-off to note: no MagSafe support. Since the case uses a two-piece design with a button assembly on the lower half, it's basically impossible to add MagSafe functionality. So if you insist on your case having MagSafe, this product might not be for you. That said, if you have MagSafe accessories (I have quite a few myself), you just need to easily remove the case to use them. Additionally, there's no protective cover for the camera control button—not a big deal, but worth noting.

Pricing and Availability

GAMEBABY is now available on BitmoLab's official website and Amazon, starting at $24.99. Three versions are offered: GameBaby Color, GameBaby Retro, and the latest GameBaby Transparent (which is what I'm showing here). The GameBaby Transparent is only available for the iPhone 17 Pro Max, with a limited production of 500 units, and can only be purchased from BitmoLab's official website. The other versions are compatible with iPhone 15 Pro and above, and can be bought on Amazon and the official website. To emphasize again, since there are no electronic components, batteries, or Bluetooth modules, they can keep the price down to $25, which is an absolute steal for a case like this!

Conclusion

If you're like me and enjoy revisiting retro games on your iPhone, this case is absolutely the perfect choice. It's affordable, lightweight and portable, easy to set up, and genuinely enhances the experience of playing retro emulator games on the iPhone. Using physical buttons combined with the iPhone's excellent haptic engine, it feels like operating a real retro game console. With the recent retro Pokémon game modding craze on social media, now is the perfect time to sit back and enjoy these games with physical buttons on your iPhone.

What do you think of this case? Would you consider getting one? Have you used one before? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section below!
